(o) ACTION
1-103. The President shall designate the Chairperson of the Council. 
1-2. Functions o f the Council. .  i
1-201. The Council shall work with Executive agencies to involve all 
sectors of the Nation, including State, county and local governments, regional 
bodies, the private sector, neighborhood groups, and volunteer and civic 
associations, in a partnership to conserve and strengthen America’s communi­
ties.
1-202. The Council shall facilitate cooperation and coordination of urban 
and regional policy implementation among and between Executive agencies.
1— 203. The Council shall assist Executive agencies in coordinating timely 
responses to State, county and local government and community development 
strategies.
1-204. The Council shall identify and seek to solve interagency and 
intergovernmental problems which impede the effective functioning of the 
Federal system.
1-205. The functions of the Council shall neither substitute for nor 
replace Executive Office of the President clearance, review and decisionmaking 
procedures.
FEDERAL REGISTER, VO L. 43, N O . 161— FRIDAY, AUG UST 18, 1978

=== PDF page 292 of 296 ===
36878 THE PRESIDENT
1-3. Administrative Provisions.
1-301. Executive agencies shall cooperate with and assist the Council in 
performing its functions.
i-302. The Chairperson shall be responsible for providing the Council 
with such administrative services or support as may be necessary or appropri­
ate.
1-303. The Chairperson may establish working groups or subcommittees 
of the Council. The Chairman may invite representatives of nonmember agen­
cies to participate from time to time in the functions of the Council.
1-304. The Chairperson shall report to the President on the performance 
of the Council’s functions.

versions.research_rationale: Version2 corrects the rejected first candidate without changing its frozen files or provisional status. The complete original has twelve numbered operative provisions; its single roster is now split into five contiguous groups, giving sixteen inventory units and isolating HEW and CSA. The Council and its broad functions have no sunset or report-triggered expiry. EO12148 adds FEMA effective July15,1979 under its express section6; it does not end existing roster commands. EO 12149 section 1-204 sends unresolved regional problems to the ICC; section 1-301 assigns ICC/OMB regional-council policy, guidance and referrals, including guidance to Federal Cochairmen; section 1-303 permits ICC requests for joint staff. These are concrete additional duties under EO 12149. EO 12314 section 4(b) expressly revokes that order and section 3 locates regional-council oversight in OMB on July 22, 1981. It neither names EO 12075 nor states that the ICC is abolished. Its narrower regional-council administration is compatible with original 1-201 to 1-204 assistance, coordination and problem-solving across executive agencies and community sectors; 1-205 already preserves EOP clearance/review/decisionmaking. Thus 1981 ends the separately added duties, not every original broad command. General support, working-group power and reporting remain tied to the surviving original Council functions. EO 12407 later revokes EO 12314 on February 22, 1983 without recreating ICC or EO 12149 duties. The HEW lead concerns name/succession after a concrete reorganization, whereas the CSA lead concerns abolition and transfer. Actual statutory texts remain unavailable, so first_end is null only for these two original seat units and savings/search closure is withheld. Fourteen other original units retain August17,1982 under the complete EO12379 section14 revocation and signature. The whole-order end remains that date because independently continuing broad Council commands end then; unresolved seats may have ended earlier but are not asserted to outlast revocation. No 1981 date is mechanically assigned to original commands, and the generic 1982 inactivity preamble supplies no earlier legal date. All legal source readings are held official extracts with official GPO fixity; editorial roster notes are explicitly leads, not originals. Complete acceptance is not requested.

versions.research_rationale: The full two-page official EO 12075 extract establishes an indefinite interagency council and twelve operative provisions; source-generator boilerplate, headings and page furniture in the machine draft have been removed, and merged 1-202/1-203 and 1-301/1-302 provisions split. No clause has a sunset, deadline, report-triggered expiry, or separate completed repeal. Section 1-304 is a continuing report duty, not a termination trigger. The actual earlier source EO 12148 section 5-210 adds FEMA to the open-ended membership in 1-102; it neither substitutes the existing roster nor ends an original command. Section 6 expressly makes that addition effective July 15, 1979, rather than July 20 signature or July 24 publication. Its emergency-function savings in 2-302 are confined to section 1 transfers, not this Council membership amendment. The complete EO 12379 section 14 then revokes EO 12075 as amended, with immediate wording and August 17, 1982 signature and no delayed effectiveness or savings. Generic inactivity in the cleanup preamble does not legally terminate these indefinite authorities; no actual earlier contrary instrument is identified in the bounded OFR/saved-text searches. The two current-law hits are historical notes for the membership amendment and revocation, not continuing predicates. Original 1-205 reserves pre-existing EOP procedures and supplies no independently surviving directive. On that target-specific chronology, August 17, 1982 is the first supported legal end of all original commands and the whole order. This is a producer conclusion for independent review, not a human certification; the USC search limitation to October 9 remains explicit and is complemented by the cutoff eCFR and later-EO scopes.

savings_residuals.reason: Within the complete original, the actual amending order and revoker, and the accepted numbered-EO/current-law search scopes, no continuing independent EO 12075 command or express saving is identified. Original 1-205 limits Council action so it does not replace EOP clearance, review and decisionmaking; it does not create a new independent EOP authority. Original 1-301 to 1-304 cooperation, support, working groups and reporting serve this Council and have no separate post-termination direction. EO 12148 section 2-302 preserves only functions transferred by that order section 1; adding FEMA to this Council under 5-210 is not such a transfer. EO 12379 revokes EO 12075 as amended without reservation. Historical administrative acts and independently existing EOP procedures are not treated as continued Council commands.

versions.research_rationale: Version2 corrects the rejected first candidate without changing its frozen files or provisional status. The complete original has twelve numbered operative provisions; its single roster is now split into five contiguous groups, giving sixteen inventory units and isolating HEW and CSA. The Council and its broad functions have no sunset or report-triggered expiry. EO12148 adds FEMA effective July15,1979 under its express section6; it does not end existing roster commands. EO 12149 section 1-204 sends unresolved regional problems to the ICC; section 1-301 assigns ICC/OMB regional-council policy, guidance and referrals, including guidance to Federal Cochairmen; section 1-303 permits ICC requests for joint staff. These are concrete additional duties under EO 12149. EO 12314 section 4(b) expressly revokes that order and section 3 locates regional-council oversight in OMB on July 22, 1981. It neither names EO 12075 nor states that the ICC is abolished. Its narrower regional-council administration is compatible with original 1-201 to 1-204 assistance, coordination and problem-solving across executive agencies and community sectors; 1-205 already preserves EOP clearance/review/decisionmaking. Thus 1981 ends the separately added duties, not every original broad command. General support, working-group power and reporting remain tied to the surviving original Council functions. EO 12407 later revokes EO 12314 on February 22, 1983 without recreating ICC or EO 12149 duties. The HEW lead concerns name/succession after a concrete reorganization, whereas the CSA lead concerns abolition and transfer. Actual statutory texts remain unavailable, so first_end is null only for these two original seat units and savings/search closure is withheld. Fourteen other original units retain August17,1982 under the complete EO12379 section14 revocation and signature. The whole-order end remains that date because independently continuing broad Council commands end then; unresolved seats may have ended earlier but are not asserted to outlast revocation. No 1981 date is mechanically assigned to original commands, and the generic 1982 inactivity preamble supplies no earlier legal date. All legal source readings are held official extracts with official GPO fixity; editorial roster notes are explicitly leads, not originals. Complete acceptance is not requested.
